title: Let's Learn English Level 2 Lesson 16
subtitle: Find Your Joy!
attribution: Source: VOA Learning English – Let's Learn English Level 2, Lesson 16: Find Your Joy! (learningenglish.voanews.com). Public domain. This unofficial study helper is not affiliated with VOA.

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.en: Hi, Kaveh! Let’s go to lunch!
dialogue.zh: 嗨，卡維！一起去吃午飯吧！

dialogue.speaker: Kaveh
dialogue.en: Ooh, I know a great place. When I first started working here, I would go every day!
dialogue.zh: 哦，我知道一個很棒的地方。我剛來這兒工作時，每天都會去！

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.en: Great. Oh, no.
dialogue.zh: 太好了。哦，不。

dialogue.speaker: Kaveh
dialogue.en: What’s wrong?
dialogue.zh: 怎麼了？

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.en: I lost my key! I just had it this morning.
dialogue.zh: 我鑰匙丟了！早上還在的。

dialogue.speaker: Kaveh
dialogue.en: You should check the Lost & Found office.
dialogue.zh: 你該去失物招領處看看。

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.en: Great idea. Where is it?
dialogue.zh: 好主意。在哪兒？

dialogue.speaker: Kaveh
dialogue.en: Oh, it used to be across from the cafeteria. But now it’s down in the basement next to the elevators. It’s really hard to find.
dialogue.zh: 哦，以前在食堂對面。現在在地下室，電梯旁邊。真的很難找。

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.en: The Lost & Found is hard to find. That’s funny.
dialogue.zh: 失物招領處很難找。好笑。

dialogue.speaker: Kaveh
dialogue.en: It is.
dialogue.zh: 是啊。

dialogue.speaker: Professor Bot
dialogue.en: I hope Anna can find the Lost & Found office! Used to and would describe something that happened repeatedly in the past. Kaveh uses would when he says, “When I first started working here, I would go every day!” There are two differences between used to and would. Number 1: We use would only when we say the time period first. Number 2: For verbs like be, think, feel, see and understand, we can only use used to. Kaveh says, “It used to be across from the cafeteria.” Keep listening for more!
dialogue.zh: 希望安娜能找到失物招領處！used to 和 would 都表示過去反覆發生的事。卡維說：“When I first started working here, I would go every day!” used to 和 would 有兩點不同。第一：只有先說出時間段時才用 would。第二：be、think、feel、see、understand 這類動詞只能用 used to。卡維說：“It used to be across from the cafeteria.” 繼續聽！

dialogue.speaker: Serenity
dialogue.en: Come in! I am Serenity.
dialogue.zh: 請進！我是寧靜。

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.en: Hi, Serenity. I’m Anna!
dialogue.zh: 嗨，寧靜。我是安娜！

dialogue.speaker: Serenity
dialogue.en: Please, sit down. How can I help you?
dialogue.zh: 請坐。我能幫你什麼？

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.en: I lost something very important.
dialogue.zh: 我丟了一件很重要的東西。

dialogue.speaker: Serenity
dialogue.en: Shh. I already know. You need help.
dialogue.zh: 噓。我已經知道了。你需要幫助。

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.en: Yes. I need help finding the key …
dialogue.zh: 是的。我需要幫忙找鑰匙……

dialogue.speaker: Serenity
dialogue.en: Shh. You need to find the key – the key that will give you happiness.
dialogue.zh: 噓。你需要找到那把鑰匙——能給你幸福的鑰匙。

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.en: Yes. Finding this key will make me very happy.
dialogue.zh: 是的。找到這把鑰匙會讓我很高興。

dialogue.speaker: Serenity
dialogue.en: First, Anna, let me tell you a little bit about myself.
dialogue.zh: 首先，安娜，讓我先說說我自己。

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.en: Okay.
dialogue.zh: 好。

dialogue.speaker: Serenity
dialogue.en: I used to be a very important person with a very important job. I made a lot of money – I mean a lot.
dialogue.zh: 我曾經是個很重要的人，有很重要的工作。我賺很多錢——我是說很多。

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.en: Wow. Good for you!
dialogue.zh: 哇。真為你高興！

dialogue.speaker: Serenity
dialogue.en: No! No, it was bad for me. I lost the most important thing – the key! You’ve lost it too, haven’t you, Anna? Haven’t you?
dialogue.zh: 不！不，那對我不好。我失去了最重要的東西——那把鑰匙！你也失去了，對不對，安娜？對不對？

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.en: I guess. So, how does this work? Do I have to fill out a form or something?
dialogue.zh: 大概吧。那這怎麼弄？我要填表還是怎樣？

dialogue.speaker: Serenity
dialogue.en: No. No forms. Just answer this one question: As a child, what did you use to do to feel happy?
dialogue.zh: 不用。不用填表。只回答一個問題：小時候，你常常做什麼才會覺得快樂？

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.en: When I was little, I used to sing all the time with my family. Those were good times.
dialogue.zh: 我小時候常常和家人一起唱歌。那是美好的時光。

dialogue.speaker: Serenity
dialogue.en: Singing is so joyful! I used to sing. But now that I’ve started my business, I’ve just been too busy. Too busy! Anna, why don’t you sing again?
dialogue.zh: 唱歌真快樂！我以前也唱歌。可自從我開始做生意，我就太忙了。太忙了！安娜，你為什麼不再唱呢？

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.en: I sing everywhere! I sing in the office. I sing on the metro. I sing in the elevators. I sing on the escalators. I sing in the bathroom. Serenity! Serenity! I really need to find my key. Yeah!
dialogue.zh: 我到處都唱！我在辦公室唱。我在地鐵上唱。我在電梯裡唱。我在扶梯上唱。我在洗手間唱。寧靜！寧靜！我真的需要找到我的鑰匙。對！

dialogue.speaker: Serenity
dialogue.en: Yes, we need to find the key … the key to happiness.
dialogue.zh: 是的，我們需要找到那把鑰匙……幸福的鑰匙。

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.en: No, no. I just need to find the key to my apartment.
dialogue.zh: 不，不。我只需要找到公寓鑰匙。

dialogue.speaker: Serenity
dialogue.en: I used to know. But now I don’t! Do you, Anna?
dialogue.zh: 我以前知道。可現在不知道了！你知道嗎，安娜？

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.en: I don’t know. I think I left it in the ladies’ room. You know, this isn’t the Lost & Found, is it?
dialogue.zh: 我不知道。我想我落在女洗手間了。你知道，這兒不是失物招領處，對吧？

dialogue.speaker: Serenity
dialogue.en: It could be the Lost & Found. I’m lost! And I used to find joy for people! I used to find joy!
dialogue.zh: 這兒也可以是失物招領處。我迷路了！我以前幫人找到快樂！我以前找到快樂！

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.en: You know, this is a bad time for you. I’ll find the Lost & Found myself. Bye, thanks.
dialogue.zh: 你現在不太方便。我會自己去找失物招領處。再見，謝謝。

dialogue.speaker: Serenity
dialogue.en: I used to find joy. I used to find joy! I used to find joy!
dialogue.zh: 我以前找到快樂。我以前找到快樂！我以前找到快樂！

dialogue.speaker: Anna
dialogue.en: Ah, I found my key!
dialogue.zh: 啊，我找到鑰匙了！

dialogue.speaker: Serenity
dialogue.en: I used to find joy!
dialogue.zh: 我以前找到快樂！

dialogue.speaker: Professor Bot
dialogue.en: Oh no. Serenity lost her joy. But at least Anna found her key! Check out our website for more!
dialogue.zh: 哦不。寧靜失去了她的快樂。不過至少安娜找到了鑰匙！去我們的網站看更多吧！

quiz.prompt: Who does Anna meet when she walks into the wrong office?
As a child, what did Anna use to do to feel happy?
